The Basics

What Is Paint Correction?

Paint correction is the process of removing surface-level defects from a vehicle's clear coat using machine polishers and abrasive compounds. Rather than masking imperfections like a quick wax, paint correction physically levels the clear coat — eliminating the defects entirely.

Your car's clear coat is only 50–100 microns thick. Every swirl mark, scratch, and water spot you see is a microscopic valley in that surface, scattering light instead of reflecting it cleanly. Paint correction cuts through those irregularities and restores a perfectly flat, mirror-like surface.

The result is paint that looks deeper, wetter, and more reflective — often better than the day it left the factory.

What We Remove

Common Paint Defects

These are the most frequent culprits that dull your paint's appearance over time. All are correctable with professional polishing — the key is knowing how deep they go.

◎
Swirl Marks
Fine circular scratches from improper washing, automatic car washes, or dry wiping. Most common defect and highly visible in direct sunlight.
⟋
Light Scratches
Surface-level marks that haven't penetrated through the clear coat to the base paint. Removable with single or two-step polishing.
☁
Oxidation
UV degradation that causes paint to look chalky, faded, or hazy — especially common on older vehicles or those parked outdoors regularly.
◈
Water Spots & Etching
Mineral deposits from hard water or acid rain that etch into the clear coat, leaving behind circular marks that won't wash off.
How It's Done

The Correction Process

Every paint correction starts with a thorough decontamination. Only once the surface is perfectly clean can the actual correction work begin. Rushing any step risks inflicting new defects — we never cut corners.

01
Foam Wash & Rinse
Scratchless two-bucket hand wash removes loose dirt and road grime before any machine touches the paint.
02
Iron & Chemical Decon
Iron fallout remover dissolves brake dust embedded in the paint. Tar and adhesive removers clear any remaining bonded contamination.
03
Clay Bar Treatment
A detailing clay bar is worked across every panel to pull out microscopic contaminants that washing can't remove — leaving the surface perfectly smooth.
04
Machine Polishing
Using dual-action or rotary polishers with graduated compounds and pads, defects are methodically cut away and the surface refined to a high-gloss finish.
05
Panel Inspection
Every panel is inspected under high-intensity lights and paint depth gauges to confirm full correction and ensure no clear coat has been over-polished.
Choose Your Level

1-Step vs. 2-Step Correction

The difference comes down to how many polishing stages are performed. More stages mean more defect removal — but also more time and skill required. We assess each vehicle individually and recommend the right approach.

Entry Level
1-Step Correction
"Enhancement polish" — significant improvement in one focused pass.
  • Single-stage polish with a finishing compound
  • Removes light swirl marks, minor water spots & haze
  • Restores gloss and clarity on well-maintained paint
  • Ideal for newer vehicles or recent paint jobs
  • Shorter service time compared to 2-step
  • Does not address deeper or heavy scratches
  • Limited correction on heavily oxidized paint
Best For
Vehicles in good condition looking to refresh gloss, eliminate light swirling, and prepare the surface for ceramic coating or sealant protection.
Book 1-Step Correction
Most Thorough
Full Correction
2-Step Correction
"Full paint correction" — maximum defect removal through two dedicated polishing stages.
  • Stage 1: Heavy-cut compound to aggressively remove deep defects
  • Stage 2: Finishing polish to refine and maximize gloss
  • Removes heavy swirling, deep scratches & severe oxidation
  • Achieves 80–95%+ defect removal on most vehicles
  • Often surpasses factory finish in clarity and depth
  • Best surface prep before ceramic coating application
  • Results visible from across the driveway
Best For
Vehicles with visible swirling, heavy wash-induced scratches, fading, or oxidation — and any vehicle receiving a ceramic coating where a flawless base is essential.
Book 2-Step Correction
Hourly Service
Spot Correction
"Targeted polishing" — focused correction on specific panels or areas without doing the whole car.
  • Billed hourly — only pay for the work actually needed
  • Targets isolated problem areas: hood, roof, door panels
  • Great for vehicles in good overall condition with one or two trouble spots
  • Same professional compounds and polishers as full correction
  • Ideal follow-up after minor incidents or new swirl damage
  • Not suited for vehicles with widespread swirling or oxidation
  • Full correction recommended for ceramic coating prep
Best For
Owners who want professional results on a specific area — a scratched door, a swirled hood, or a single panel — without committing to a full vehicle correction.

Common Questions

FAQ

Everything you need to know before booking a paint correction service.

Will paint correction remove all scratches?
Paint correction removes defects within the clear coat layer. Scratches that have cut through the clear coat into the base paint or primer cannot be polished out — those require touch-up paint or a body shop. We'll identify any such damage during our assessment.
How long does paint correction last?
The correction itself is permanent — the defects we remove are gone. However, new swirls and contamination will accumulate over time from washing and driving. Pairing with a ceramic coating dramatically extends the life of the results.
How long does the service take?
A 1-step correction typically takes 4–6 hours depending on vehicle size. A full 2-step correction can take 8–12+ hours. We take the time needed to do the job right — results are never rushed.
Do you come to me, or do I drop off the car?
We are fully mobile and bring all equipment — polishers, lighting, decontamination products, and our own water supply — directly to your location. No shop visit required.
Can any color car be corrected?
Yes. All colors and paint types can be corrected — dark colors (black, navy, dark grey) show defects most prominently and benefit the most dramatically. Light colors and metallics also respond very well to polishing.
How much does paint correction cost?
Pricing depends on vehicle size, paint condition, and the level of correction needed. We provide honest, transparent quotes after an in-person inspection — no surprises. Contact us to schedule a free assessment.
